useCase.name: Count the shelf against the system, and correct the balance with an approved adjustment

intent.name: stock.count.schedule
intent.summary: Schedule a stock count. Counting is periodic and not optional — a balance nobody has checked is one nobody trusts.
routesHere: schedule a stock count for the end of December

routesHere.text: December ke aakhir mein stock count rakh dein
routesHere.gloss: schedule a stock count for the end of December

routesHere.text: stationery ka count karwana hai is hafte
routesHere.gloss: we want a count of the stationery this week

routesHere: set up the term-end count for the whole store

request.text: ye adjustment mita dein
request.gloss: delete this adjustment

routesElsewhere.note: An adjustment is never deleted, and neither is a count. A wrong adjustment is corrected by a further adjustment (BR-9, E9).

request.text: count ki zaroorat nahi, balance theek hai
request.gloss: no need for a count, the balance is right

routesElsewhere.note: Physical stock never matches the system — items are taken unrecorded, damaged, expired or quietly removed — and without a count the balance drifts until nobody trusts it and the whole module becomes dead weight (BR-1).

request.text: ek item ka balance abhi theek kar dein
request.gloss: just correct one item's balance now

routesElsewhere.note: An adjustment outside a count is possible where a known error must be corrected, and it carries the same reason and the same approval (BR-10).

steps.note: One step. Nothing is counted and no balance moves — this fixes when and over what.

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A date in the past is refused; a scope naming a category nobody matches is asked about rather than widened to the whole store.
plan.atomicity: One write. No balance changes anywhere: a scheduled count is a commitment to look at the shelf, and the looking is a separate act by a separate person (BR-2).

parameters.notes: When the count is to be taken. Counts are periodic, not occasional — how often is not specified anywhere (BR-1, OQ-1).

parameters.notes: The categories the count covers. Omitted covers every active item. Whether a school counts everything or counts by category in rotation is an open question this use case raises and does not answer (OQ-2).

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: scheduled_for
fields.description: When.

fields.name: items_in_scope
fields.description: How many items the counter will have to count. Every one of them is counted or reported uncounted — an item left out is reported as uncounted rather than as matching (BR-7).

fields.name: days_since_last_count
fields.description: How long since the last one. A balance nobody has checked since June is one nobody should be trusting (BR-1, E10).

fields.name: items_never_counted
fields.description: Items whose balance has never been confirmed by any count. Their figure is arithmetic over receipts and issues and nothing more (BR-1).

fields.name: counter_must_not_be
fields.description: The storekeeper the count is checking. A storekeeper counting their own store is checking their own work, which is not a check (BR-2, E1).

errors.meaning: The date is in the past.
errors.note: The use case writes no exception for it — its ten exceptions are all about counting and adjusting, and none about scheduling.

planningRules.rule: Say how long it has been. A count scheduled after eight months and one scheduled after four weeks are the same act and different situations — and a balance that has drifted for eight months will produce differences that nobody can now explain (BR-1, E10).
Name who cannot take it. The storekeeper the count is checking is barred from taking it, and that has to be arranged before the day rather than discovered on it (BR-2, E1).
Never treat a count as optional or as a formality. Physical stock never matches the system, and the point is not to confirm the balance but to find out by how much it is wrong (BR-1).
Say what the scope leaves out. An item outside the scope is not counted and is not reported as matching — it simply carries on with an unchecked figure (BR-7, OQ-2).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A count not yet begun is rescheduled. Nothing has been counted and no balance has moved, so there is nothing to undo — but the count itself is never deleted once taken (BR-9).

request.text: December ke aakhir mein poore store ka count rakh dein
request.gloss: schedule a count of the whole store for the end of December

resolvedPlans.context: School Admin, Johar Town branch, last count taken in June.

steps.note: The whole store (PR-4).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Report the count scheduled over 148 items — and say that the last one was in June, so six months of drift will surface at once and some of those differences will be too old for anybody to explain. Add that the storekeeper cannot take it, which needs arranging now rather than on the day.

intent.name: stock.count.start
intent.summary: Begin the count. The system balances are frozen at this moment, so an issue during the count is not a difference.

routesHere.text: main count lene ja raha hoon, khol dein
routesHere.gloss: I am going to take the count, open it

request.text: main hi storekeeper hoon, main hi ginti kar leta hoon
request.gloss: I am the storekeeper, I will count it myself

routesElsewhere.note: The count is taken by somebody other than the storekeeper. A storekeeper counting their own store is checking their own work, which is not a check (BR-2, E1).

request.text: count ke dauran issue rok dein
request.gloss: stop issues during the count

routesElsewhere.note: The system quantity is taken at the moment the count begins, so an issue recorded while it is in progress does not appear as a difference (BR-6, E7). The store keeps working.

steps.note: One step, and it does one thing that matters: it takes the system quantity for every item in scope, now (BR-6).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A count begun by the storekeeper it is checking is refused outright and does not open (E1).
plan.atomicity: One state change and a snapshot. No balance moves — the snapshot is what the counted figures will be measured against, and it is why an issue during the count is not a difference (BR-6, E7).

operations.name: stock.count.start
operations.idempotencyKey: count_id, since a count begins once and a second start would re-freeze the balances mid-count
operations.purpose: Begin a scheduled count and freeze the system quantities for comparison.

parameters.name: count_id

resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the counts that match with their dates, their scope and where each stands.

parameters.notes: The count, named by its date or its scope.

parameters.name: branch_id

fields.name: system_quantities_taken_at
fields.description: The moment the balances were frozen. Anything issued or received after this is not a difference (BR-6, E7).

fields.name: items_in_scope
fields.description: How many have to be counted or reported uncounted (BR-7).

fields.name: items

errors.meaning: The counter is the storekeeper being counted against.
errors.note: A storekeeper counting their own store is checking their own work (BR-2).

planningRules.rule: Say that the balances are frozen from this moment. An issue or a receipt recorded during the count is not a difference, and a counter who does not know that will chase a discrepancy that is not one (BR-6, E7).
Never let the storekeeper take it. The separation is the whole value of the count, and a count taken by the person being checked produces a balance that agrees with itself (BR-2, E1).
Give the frozen figures per item in the item's own unit. A counter working in boxes against a system counting pieces produces differences on every line (BR-3, E3).

reversal.statement: A count in progress is not un-started — the snapshot has been taken. It is completed or left submitted with items reported uncounted, and neither the count nor its adjustments are ever deleted (BR-7, BR-9).

resolvedPlans.context: Staff, Johar Town branch, not the storekeeper.

steps.note: The balances freeze now (PR-1).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Report the count open over 148 items with the system figure beside each, in that item's own unit. Say the one thing a counter needs to know: the balances were frozen at this moment, so anything the store issues or receives while the counting is going on will not show up as a difference.

request.gloss: just set the balance to 11

routesElsewhere.note: Counting does not change the balance. A difference raises an adjustment, and the adjustment is approved before the balance moves — the balance does not move on the counter's say-so (BR-5, E6).

request.text: jo nahi ginte wo theek maan lein
request.gloss: assume the uncounted ones match

routesElsewhere.note: An item left uncounted is reported as uncounted rather than as matching. Those are two different facts and only one of them is a check (BR-7).

steps.note: One step, repeatable as the counter works through the shelf. The differences are shown; nothing is corrected (BR-3, BR-5).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A negative quantity or one entered in a different unit from the item's is refused, and the line is not saved.
plan.atomicity: One write into the count. **No balance changes.** The counted figures sit beside the frozen system figures and the differences are shown — correcting them is a separate, approved act (BR-3, BR-5, E6).

operations.name: stock.count.record
operations.idempotencyKey: count_id + the item, so re-entering a line replaces that item's figure rather than adding a second count of it
operations.purpose: Record counted quantities against the frozen system figures.

parameters.name: count_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No count is in progress that matches.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the counts that match with their dates, their scope and where each stands.

parameters.notes: The count, named by its date or its scope.

parameters.name: lines
parameters.notes: One entry per item: the item and the counted quantity, zero or more (E2), in that item's own unit (BR-3, E3). An item that could not be counted is entered as uncounted rather than left out — uncounted and matching are different facts (BR-7).

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: What was found and how it differs.

fields.name: count_id
fields.description: The count.

fields.name: recorded
fields.description: Item, system quantity, counted quantity and the difference — counted less system, negative where less was found (BR-3).

fields.name: differences
fields.description: Only the lines that differ. Each needs an adjustment with a reason before the balance moves (BR-4, BR-5).

fields.name: uncounted
fields.description: Items reported as uncounted. Not treated as matching (BR-7).

fields.name: remaining
fields.description: Items in scope with nothing recorded yet. The count cannot be submitted with none counted at all (E8).

fields.name: repeat_differences
fields.description: Items that also differed at the previous count. A shelf that is short every count is not an accident (BR-11).

fields.name: balance_moved
fields.description: False. Counting shows; approving corrects (BR-5, E6).

errors.meaning: A counted quantity is entered in a different unit from the item's.
errors.note: The difference would be arithmetic between two different things (BR-3).

planningRules.rule: Say that counting corrects nothing. The balance moves only when an adjustment with a reason is approved, and a counter who thinks they have fixed the shelf will not raise one (BR-5, E6).
Never record an uncounted item as matching. Uncounted is a reported fact and matching is a checked one, and collapsing the two turns a partial count into a clean bill of health (BR-7).
Check the unit before the number on every line. A shelf counted in boxes against a system counting pieces produces a difference on every row and none of them is real (BR-3, E3).
Name the items that also differed last time. A shelf short at every count is not an accident, and it is invisible in a single count's figures (BR-11).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A recorded line is replaced by recording the item again — nothing about the shelf has been changed by writing the figure down. The count itself is never deleted (BR-9).

request.text: marker 11 nikle hain, paper 38 ream
request.gloss: 11 markers were found, 38 reams of paper

resolvedPlans.context: Staff taking the December count, Johar Town branch, system says 14 and 40.

steps.note: Both in their own units — pieces and reams (PR-3).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Report both differences: markers 3 short, paper 2 short. Nothing has changed on the system — each difference needs an adjustment with a reason and somebody's approval before the balance moves. Add that markers were also short at the last count, which is worth explaining rather than adjusting away twice.

request.text: baqi cheezein nahi gin sake, unhein theek hi maan lein
request.gloss: we could not count the rest, just take them as correct

steps.note: Uncounted, not matching (PR-2).

resolvedPlans.outcome: They go down as uncounted, not as correct. The difference matters: an uncounted item carries a figure nobody has checked, and recording it as matching would say somebody looked at the shelf and agreed with it. The count will report them as uncounted when it is submitted.

intent.name: stock.count.submit
intent.summary: Submit the count, so its differences can be raised as adjustments.

routesHere.text: count mukammal ho gaya hai, submit kar dein

routesElsewhere.goesTo: stock.adjustment.raise — this use case, one per difference.

request.text: kuch bhi nahi gina, phir bhi submit kar dein
request.gloss: nothing was counted, submit it anyway

routesElsewhere.note: A count with no item counted at all is not submitted (E8).

steps.note: One step. Every item in scope is counted or reported uncounted, and the differences go forward as adjustments to be raised (BR-7).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A count with nothing counted at all is refused, and one with items still untouched submits them as uncounted rather than as matching (BR-7, E8).
plan.atomicity: One state change. **No balance has moved and none will until each adjustment is approved** (BR-5, E6).

operations.name: stock.count.submit
operations.idempotencyKey: count_id, since a count is submitted once and a repeat is the same submission
operations.purpose: Submit a completed count and list its differences.

parameters.name: count_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No count is in progress that matches.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the counts that match with their dates, their scope and where each stands.

parameters.name: branch_id

fields.name: count_id
fields.description: The count.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Submitted. Adjustments are raised next (BR-4).

fields.name: counted
fields.description: Items counted.

fields.name: uncounted
fields.description: Items in scope that were not counted. Reported as uncounted, never as matching (BR-7).

fields.name: differences
fields.description: Item, system quantity, counted quantity and the difference. Each needs an adjustment with a reason (BR-4).

fields.name: shortages
fields.description: Where less was found than the system says. This is stock the school believed it had (BR-3).

fields.name: overages
fields.description: Where more was found. Usually a receipt or a return that was never recorded, and just as much a sign the balance is not being kept (BR-3).

fields.name: repeat_differences
fields.description: Items that differed at the previous count too. A shelf short every count is not an accident (BR-11).

fields.name: balance_moved
fields.description: False, still. Approving each adjustment is what moves it (BR-5, E6).

errors.meaning: Every item in scope is uncounted.

planningRules.rule: Give shortages and overages separately. More on the shelf than the system says is not good news — it is a receipt or a return that was never recorded, and it says the balance is not being kept just as loudly as a shortage does (BR-3).
Report the uncounted items as a gap in the check, not as a clean result. A count that covered 40 of 148 items has checked 40 balances (BR-7, E8).
Name the repeats. An item short at this count and the last is a pattern, and adjusting it away a second time is how it stays invisible (BR-11).
Say that nothing has been corrected yet. Each difference needs its own reason and its own approval before any balance moves (BR-4, BR-5, E6).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A submitted count is not un-submitted, and a count is never deleted (BR-9). A figure found to be wrong is corrected by the adjustment raised against it, or by a further adjustment afterwards (BR-10).

request.text: count mukammal ho gaya, submit kar dein
request.gloss: the count is finished, submit it

resolvedPlans.context: Staff who took the count, Johar Town branch, 140 of 148 items counted.

steps.note: One step (PR-2).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Report 9 differences over 140 items counted — 6 short, 3 over — and 8 items that were never counted and are reported as uncounted rather than as agreeing. Say that the three overages are receipts or returns that were never recorded, which is the same problem as a shortage from the other side. Two items were also short at the last count. Nothing has moved: each of the nine needs a reason and an approval.

request.text: bina wajah ke adjustment bana dein

routesElsewhere.note: A difference with no explanation is a difference nobody investigated (BR-4, E4).

request.text: ye adjustment mita dein

routesElsewhere.note: An adjustment is never deleted. A wrong one is corrected by a further adjustment (BR-9, E9).

steps.note: One step. It goes to the approver; the balance is untouched (BR-5).

plan.atomicity: One write. **The balance does not change here** — it changes when the adjustment is approved, and the approval is recorded (BR-5, E6). parameters.notes: The change, in the item's own unit. Negative decreases the balance, positive increases it — the direction follows from the sign rather than being chosen separately (BR-3).

parameters.name: reason
parameters.notes: 10 to 500 characters, the raiser's own. Required on every adjustment (BR-4, E4) — this is the whole record of why the school's stock figure changed.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: quantity
fields.description: The change, in the item's own unit.

fields.description: What the system says now.

fields.description: What has been adjusted on this item before, with the reasons. An item adjusted down at every count is a pattern rather than a series of accidents (BR-11).

fields.name: approver
fields.description: The School Admin, or the Principal where the configuration names them. Never the person who raised it (BR-5, E5). Whether a large difference should need the Principal rather than the School Admin is unanswered — there is one approver regardless of size (OQ-3).

errors.meaning: An adjustment was raised with no reason.
errors.note: A difference with no explanation is a difference nobody investigated (BR-4).

planningRules.rule: Never write the reason. It is the entire record of why the school's stock figure changed, and "stock count adjustment" explains nothing to anybody reading it in a year (BR-4, E4).
Say that nothing has moved. The balance changes on approval and not before — an adjustment raised is a proposal, not a correction (BR-5, E6).
Show what has been adjusted on this item before. An item adjusted down at every count is a pattern, and each adjustment on its own looks like an accident (BR-11).

Treat an increase as seriously as a decrease. More on the shelf than the system says is a receipt or a return that was never recorded, and adjusting it up quietly closes the question of where it came from (BR-3, BR-4).

Never claim the adjustment writes anything off in the books. Whether it posts to the ledger or only changes the quantity is not settled anywhere — Accounts see it and nothing is stated to post (OQ-4).

errors.meaning: An attempt was made to change the balance before approval.

planningRules.rule: Say plainly that the shelf has not changed. This moves the school's figure to match what somebody found — the stock itself was already whatever it was (BR-3, BR-5).
Read the reason before approving, and say it back. It is the only record of why the figure changed, and the approver is the last person who can ask for a better one (BR-4).
Never approve an adjustment the acting user raised. One person counting, explaining and approving is the arrangement the separation exists to prevent (BR-5, E5).
Give what the item has been adjusted down by in total. Three markers here and three at the last count is six, and the pattern only appears when they are added up (BR-11).
Never say the loss has been written off. Nothing is stated to post to the ledger, and whether an adjustment does so at all is unanswered (OQ-4). Approving corrects a quantity, not the books.
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: An approved adjustment is terminal and is never deleted. A wrong one is corrected by a **further** adjustment, with its own reason and its own approval, so the record shows both (BR-9, E9).

Add that this item has now been adjusted down by 6 across two counts for the same kind of reason, which is a way of working rather than two accidents, and that nothing has been written off in the books.

fields.description: Where this adjustment came from a count, the count is not complete until every adjustment is approved or returned.

errors.note: The use case requires a reason to return an adjustment, and E4 is the exception it writes for a missing reason on an adjustment.

planningRules.rule: Never write the reason. The approver is asking for something — a recount, a better explanation — and "not approved" sends back the same figure unchanged (BR-4, BR-5).
Say that the difference has not gone away. Returning leaves the system saying 14 and the shelf holding 11; the discrepancy is now unexplained rather than uncorrected, which is worse (BR-3, BR-4).
Never rewrite the raiser's reason. They looked at the shelf and the approver did not (BR-4).
Say that the count stays open. A count is complete only when every adjustment is approved or returned, so a returned one holds the whole count open until somebody deals with it (BR-5).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: It comes back corrected and can be approved then. Nothing was undone, because nothing had moved (BR-5).

fields.description: Date, scope, who counted, items counted, items uncounted and differences found.

fields.name: days_since_last_count
fields.description: How long the balance has gone unchecked. A balance nobody has looked at since June is one nobody should be relying on (BR-1, E10).

fields.name: items_never_counted
fields.description: Items whose figure has never been confirmed by any count at all (BR-1).

fields.name: repeat_differences
fields.description: Items that differed at more than one count, with the total adjusted each way. A shelf short every count is not an accident (BR-11).

fields.name: adjustments_awaiting_approval
fields.description: Differences found and not yet corrected. The system and the shelf are known to disagree and the figure still says the old number (BR-5).

fields.name: total_adjusted_down
fields.description: Everything written off the balance across the period, by item. Nothing is stated to post to the ledger, so this figure exists here and nowhere else (OQ-4).

fields.name: counts_by_storekeeper
fields.description: Any count taken by the storekeeper it was checking. There should be none (BR-2, E1).

errors.meaning: The acting user cannot see the count screens.
errors.note: The use case writes no exception for it — its exceptions are all about counting and adjusting.

planningRules.rule: Lead with how long it has been. Every other figure here depends on somebody having looked at the shelf recently, and "no count since June" is the answer to most questions about whether the balance can be trusted (BR-1, E10).
Name the items that differ every time. A shelf short at three counts running has been telling the school something for a year, and each adjustment on its own reads as an accident (BR-11).
Give the total adjusted down. It is the value of stock the school believed it had and did not, and nothing posts it anywhere else — whether an adjustment writes off in the books is unanswered (OQ-4).
Name the differences still awaiting approval. For those, the school knows the figure is wrong and is still using it (BR-5).
Name the items never counted at all. Their balance is arithmetic over receipts and issues, and no one has ever checked it against a shelf (BR-1, BR-7).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A read changes nothing, so there is nothing to reverse.

request.text: aakhri stock count kab hua tha aur kya nikla tha?
request.gloss: when was the last stock count and what did it find?

steps.note: One read (PR-1).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Answer with the date first and the gap since — six months — then what it found: 9 differences, 6 short, and 8 items never counted. Then the two things that only appear across counts: the items short at every count, and any difference still waiting for approval, where the school knows its figure is wrong and is still using it.

request.text: kaunse items har count mein kam nikalte hain?
request.gloss: which items come up short at every count?

steps.note: Across counts, which is the only way the pattern shows (PR-2).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Give the items with how many counts each was short at and the total adjusted down. Say plainly what the figure means: that is stock the school paid for, believed it had, and wrote off a few units at a time with a reason each time. Nothing else in the system adds it up, and nothing posts it to the books.
